title: Admit contributions atomically with grants, reservations and active commitments
goal: Create the trusted admission boundary that turns an attributable contribution and award into bounded authority without partially granting resources or responsibility.
scope: Implement Contribution/Forecast/CostEstimate, Assignment, Grant, Invocation and active Commitment/Lease values needed by admission. Use typed ContributionKind and RoleKind; preserve subject/criterion targets and proposed_by Runtime or Agent(Assignment). Validate the committed Award’s solicitation/offer/profile/subject before execution.

Implement trusted Gatekeeper.admit/revoke: pins/constraints, actual capabilities, subject/producer independence, path locks, both reserves, parallel_limit, attempt_limit, deadline and exactly one active commitment. Record AssignmentAdmitted/GrantIssued/CommitmentChanged/ReservationChanged atomically. Revoke authority immediately while retaining unresolved scoped/financial holds under their independent release conditions.

For the fixed W1 flow, implement a minimal persisted Arbiter open/submit/award path with one RuntimeProxy offer; it still records ContributionProposed/SolicitationOpened/OfferSubmitted/Awarded. Full voluntary solicitation and reopening are W3-0003.
acceptance: The real Gatekeeper consumer validates a persisted contribution/RuntimeProxy offer/award and commits one bounded Assignment/Grant/Commitment with matching resource/path ownership over MemoryJournal and durable Journal. It starts no backend by itself.

Stale/mismatched awards, invalid settings/pins, producer independence, missing capabilities, exhausted budget/limits or path conflicts yield attributable denial with no partial grant/reservation/commitment. Independent producers may share RoleKind when other rules permit.

A repeated admission cannot grant duplicate responsibility. Revoke invalidates authority without fabricating cessation or settlement; W1-0017 exercises actual starts/completion/recovery and W1-0010 owns accepted-result review integration.
context: Authority: ymp-docs/self-organizing-team-domain-model.md, sections 3.4–3.5, 4 (Gatekeeper, Arbiter), A5, P2 admission, R-2/R-3/R-4/R-5/R-8/R-9/R-12/R-14. Use the approved model with 811a872 semantics and the greenfield baseline in 0c61ff1 and §5.8 for experimental strategy boundaries. Other documents and existing names explain implementation facts only.

Greenfield: create this behavior in the new implementation. Paths below are PROPOSED target modules under the layout owned by W1-0001; only completed prerequisite tasks supply implementation. Prior source, APIs, fixtures and delivery claims are not a baseline.

Create proposed crates/ymp-domain/src/assignment.rs, crates/ymp-kernel/src/{gatekeeper,arbiter}.rs and runtime admission wiring. Dependencies supply Registry, Treasury, Direct WorkspaceGuard and atomic durable Journal. W1-0017 separately builds the execution host and Scripted backend, keeping this task sized around authority/ownership.

A minimal W1 Arbiter open/submit/award path with one RuntimeProxy offer is real persisted behavior, not a free-floating fabricated Award. W3-0003 adds all voluntary offer/deadline/reopen branches; agent-callable transport is W3-0001.

Bootstrap Plan contributions can have no committed criterion targets yet. Admission validates committed facts and typed subject references; W1-0008/0010 later supply real result/acceptance producers. W1-0007 owns the rest of P2 lifecycle. Role/Grant/Assignment IDs remain distinct from Invocation/native session.

Arbiter foundation checkpoint: typed Contribution/Forecast/Assignment/Grant/Invocation and coordination values; Prob input validation and competence mapping; persisted Runtime contributions, solicitations, RuntimeProxy offers and Awarded plus Proposed Commitment as one indivisible packet. FirstOffer and a test alternative run through the actual consumer over MemoryJournal/SQLite. The source acceptance contract Ref is retained. Unsupported typed subject references are denied until their owning services supply real typed resolution; offer/award timing follows recorded inputs and P1. Exact append resolution checks both atomic packet boundaries. Independent review ACCEPT for this intermediate checkpoint; full offline build/fmt/clippy/tests, legacy scan and task check passed. See ymp-docs/admission-implementation.md. Gatekeeper admission/revocation and live capability issuance remain unimplemented, so W1-0006 stays in progress.

Admission design review: prepare a sealed, non-serializable access plan without journalling or live handles; consume it once only after confirmed complete admission. Preserve original resource policy input by starting the attempt-bound packet with ReservationChanged, then optional matching LockChanged, GrantIssued, active CommitmentChanged and final AssignmentAdmitted. Strict order/nonce/assignment checks must prevent reuse of older standalone resources and incomplete/interleaved appends. Prepare the grant secret privately and persist only its digest. Confirmed post-commit capability-delivery failure is not an admission denial; journal data cannot recreate a second live handle/secret. No-files requires enforceable absence of file access, not merely empty declared needs. CAS conflicts cannot cancel another admission; only the exact current Proposed commitment may be cancelled on a confirmed denial. Memory no-files consumer plus explicit synthetic scoped-plan conformance is acceptable; real filesystem admission and cross-session atomicity require SQLite/WorkspaceGuard integration.
